title: CD Shoot animation cadence
symptom: The hovered language flag and later skeets animate much too quickly.
expected: Guest animation cadence remains synchronized with the 50 Hz player.
revalidation_reason: The changed scheduling prerequisite is now implemented and neighboring automated baselines pass. A 2026-08-09 manual check confirms that the hovered language flag remains correctly paced, but historical testing places that correction before the regional-clock change. The skeet sequence was not rechecked, so the incident remains open and no causal credit is assigned to the new scheduler.

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: Legacy SCC68070 instruction timing lets guest animation logic perform too much work per MCD212 frame. Restoring section-6.2 timings without cycle/event-interleaved device advancement is insufficient because that historical combination regressed The 7th Guest.
supporting_evidence: The section-6.2 timing implementation in 191eebb corrected this cadence.
Commit 18beb7f restored legacy timing to preserve The 7th Guest under the current instruction-boundary scheduler.
The bounded three-clock timeline characterized a timer deadline at cycle 96 being observed at cycle 154, 58 cycles late under instruction-boundary lumping.
The replacement scheduler services that timer in 96- and 58-cycle slices while retaining the 154-cycle instruction total.
Runtime regional cadence tests pin the documented PAL 30.0000 MHz and NTSC 30.2098 MHz crystals, exact MCD212 line/field boundaries, 75 Hz CDIC cadence, SLAVE delays, and VMPEG clocks.
The deterministic Alien Gate, The 7th Guest, and Accused compatibility baseline passes with the new scheduler and regional clocks.
contradicting_evidence: The hovered flag was already correctly paced before chronological device slicing and runtime regional clocks were introduced, so that observation cannot establish this hypothesis as the cause of the correction.
The later skeet sequence has not been manually revalidated on the current build.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Reject the implementation if synthetic deadline order, selected-clock device rates, shared-IN4 ownership, or neighboring CPU/CDIC/MCD212/DVC regressions fail. Do not claim the CD Shoot symptom fixed until a current manual PAL run confirms both flag and skeet cadence.

context.scenario: synthetic deadline/rate tests plus small deterministic neighboring-title baseline

experiments.strategy: Advance all devices to the earliest pending deadline within each completed CPU-instruction window, select the documented PAL/NTSC host clock at runtime, and retain exact instruction totals.
assumptions: A CPU cannot observe a device interrupt until the next instruction boundary.
The deterministic neighboring-title suite exercises the established shared-IN4 and sustained VMPEG paths but not CD Shoot's visible animation cadence.
experiments.expected: The synthetic 154-cycle instruction services a timer deadline at cycle 96, regional devices preserve their documented rates, and established neighboring-title checkpoints do not regress.
experiments.actual: The instruction advances devices in 96- and 58-cycle slices. One selected-clock second yields 50 PAL or 59 completed NTSC fields and 75 CDIC sector ticks. Alien Gate, sustained The 7th Guest, and native Accused pass all explicit baseline assertions; The 7th Guest reports zero DVC decoder errors.
improvements: Removed device-to-device event lumping across an instruction's elapsed window without changing SCC68070 instruction totals; CPU bus accesses remain pre-catch-up.
Applied documented regional host clocks consistently to display, disc, SLAVE, VMPEG, and frontend pacing.

conditions: Mono-I/CD-i 220 PAL or NTSC runtime selection
invalidated_by: A regression in a neighboring shared-IN4 or sustained VMPEG checkpoint
repeat_when: CD Shoot is available for a current manual PAL flag-and-skeet run
Machine device ordering or regional clock propagation changes

manual_verification.notes: The previously corrected fast language-flag animation reportedly returned.

Manual testing confirms that the hovered CD Shoot flag remains correctly paced; historical testing places this correction before the regional-clock work. The skeet sequence was not checked, so this is regression evidence only and not proof that the new scheduler fixed the title.
